column1: # mapping_set_description: DataCite 4.7 conceptual correspondences to Wikidata Q-items. This is not a DataCite-to-Wikidata
#   statement exporter. Narrow and broad matches express conceptual scope and do not license unconditional rdf:type
#   or P31 statements. Generic identifier-to-ORCID equivalence is explicitly excluded.
# comment: Curated from source definitions and official target documentation.
#   Wikidata evidence is a dated lookup, not an immutable vocabulary release.

column13: comment
The qualifier identifies an organizational name; the corresponding entity-kind concept is organization, without generating a Wikidata instance assertion.
The concepts describe books; do not infer a particular edition or physical copy.
Wikidata chapter includes divisions of works beyond books; the target concept is broader.
Both describe purposely grouped resources or objects.
Wikidata conference paper describes a document published in conference proceedings; DataCite also includes submissions intended for conference acceptance.
Both describe a collection of papers issued for an academic conference.
Both describe a scholarly publication focused on describing data.
Both describe a collection of data; this is concept alignment, not a generated Wikidata statement.
Both describe academic thesis work; qualification-level details require source preservation.
Both describe a visual representation; no file format or licensing inference is implied.
Both describe an academic periodical; preserve the source scholarly-publication context.
The Wikidata article concept also includes newspaper and magazine articles, beyond a journal article.
The Wikidata model concept includes physical and conceptual representations; DataCite Model describes abstract representations. No 3D restriction is imposed.
A data management plan covers a subset of the broader DataCite plans for research outputs, which may also include software and other outputs.
Wikidata review includes evaluations beyond scientific or professional peer review.
Both describe tangible objects; retain specific sample or material descriptions.
Both describe research posters for academic events; correspondence checked against the Wikidata conference-poster item.
Both describe a scholarly paper before formal peer-reviewed publication.
The DataCite value describes a set of slides; the matching item is a slide deck, not the delivery event or a single slide.
Both describe a planned endeavor to achieve a goal using allocated resources.
Both describe a report document; a record-level conversion still requires independent bibliographic modeling.
Both describe computer software; DataCite excludes computational notebooks and includes source code, so exact equivalence is not asserted.
Both concern recorded audio content; an audio-record conversion requires separate graph and media modeling.
Wikidata text is broader; DataCite Text excludes separately enumerated textual resource types.
Both denote an organized sequence of activities; execution metadata is outside this correspondence.
Both denote the secondary title accompanying a main title; no literal title statement is produced.
